title: Integration window slate and hourly fallback log
summary: Working notes for a 48h integration window covering a mixed-hosted/dedicated rollout. Focus areas: clear hourly guardrails, dependency matrix (infra & model variants), and a compact fallback log to capture per-hour observations and triggers.
body:
Purpose: coordinate cross-team checks (serving-runtime, infra, observability, product) during a limited integration window. This doc is intentionally compact so on-call and ship-week staff can scan and execute quickly. It contains (1) a dependency matrix, (2) an hourly cadence with owners and abort/fallback triggers, (3) a lightweight fallback log template, and (4) draft release notes artifacts to copy into the customer-facing release.

Key constraints and decisions: 
- Rollout mode: staged canary -> regional ramp -> global. Canary will be 0.5% traffic for first 2h, then 2% for next 6h, subject to telemetry gates.
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to model-variant v1-quant or region fallback when 95th latency > 900ms or error rate > 0.8% sustained for 5m.
- Cost throttle: if token/sec cost > baseline+40% and latency improvements are < 8%, pause traffic increase, notif SRE.

Open questions (to resolve before window):
- Who owns the final decision to stop ramp at 2%? (Suggested: release lead + infra on-call)
- Can Dedicated capacity autoscale during canary (yes/no)? If no, prepare manual backfill runbooks.
- Confirm KMS/HSM audit hook for private tenants (Priya to confirm).

Unresolved items and notes to self: 
- Need to add an explicit run for prefix-KV cache warmup pre-canary (30m before canary start).
- Coordinate with customer-success for any customers in the first two regions on the ramp list.
dependency_matrix: serving-runtime: model routing config (feature-flagged) — owner: Maya Li — impact: high — fallback: model-variant v1-quant
edge-proxy: gradual config push by region — owner: Oskar Jensen — impact: high — fallback: rollback to proxy vstable
autoscaler: dedicated GPU pool policies — owner: Infra Oncall — impact: medium — fallback: manual scale-add
telemetry: sampling changes for token-level latency and error-rate — owner: Observability — impact: medium — fallback: revert sampling to default
KMS/HSM: key rotation window — owner: Security — impact: low (private tenants) — fallback: delay rollout for private customers
hourly_cadence: T-0:30 — Preflight: warm caches (prefix/KV), validate smoke tests against shadowing endpoint — owner: Maya Li
T-0:10 — Team sync: 15m quick check (release lead, infra, observability, product) — owner: Release Lead
T+0h — Start canary 0.5% — monitor 5m buckets, notify on gate breaches — owner: Oncall
T+1h — Canary review: decision to continue to 2% or rollback (based on gates) — owner: Release Lead + Infra
T+3h — Ramp to 2% if gates stable for 30m — owner: Release Lead
T+6h — Regional ramp candidate: pick region B (ap-southeast) — run localized smoke tests before traffic split — owner: Oskar Jensen
Every hour — Observability snapshot: 95th latency, p99, errors, token/sec cost — owner: Observability (report into #ops-rollout)
fallback_log_template: timestamp — region — trigger_reason — immediate_action_taken — owner — postmortem_needed? (y/n)
e.g. 2026-08-12T03:40Z — us-west1 — p95 > 900ms for 10m — routed traffic to v1-quant and reduced canary to 0.2% — Maya Li — y
telemetry_and_sampling_instructions: Short: keep token-level sampling for first 6h with full traces at 1/1000, increase sampling if noise appears. Add rollout tags to all traces: release=integration-window-2026-08, canary=0.5->2.0. Observability to post hourly json-summary to the release channel.
abort_criteria: unexpected increase in token/sec cost > 40% sustained for 10m without commensurate latency reduction
inability to autoscale dedicated pools when load increases by 20% above baseline
escalation_matrix: Level 1: oncall SRE — first responder — immediate mitigation
Level 2: infra lead + release lead — decision to pause ramp/rollback
Level 3: CTO + Customer Ops — customer-facing comms and extended mitigation
quick_run_checks: Verify canary routing config applied to edge-proxies
Confirm cache warmup completed and hit-rate >= 80%
Smoke test the shadow endpoint with 10 sample prompts (expected SLOs)
Validate telemetry tags and ensure auto-posting to #ops-rollout
Confirm KMS audit hook presence for private tenant traffic
post_deploy_notes_draft:
Draft release notes (internal):
- Feature: staged rollout of model-routing improvements enabling thinner KV cache sharing across variants.
- Observability: added token-level sampling for root-cause triage and automatic rollback gates.
- Ops: new hourly snapshot reports and a compact fallback log for rapid triage.
Customer-facing summary: We're rolling out an efficiency and reliability update to model routing that reduces cold-start penalties and improves throughput. The rollout will be staged with automatic safety gates — no expected customer impact. If we detect regressions for any specific region or tenant, we'll automatically route to a stable model variant and notify affected customers.
notes_for_retrospective: Capture: gating thresholds used, false positives/negatives during canary, timeline of any fallbacks and their root cause, suggestions to improve preflight (esp. cache warmup and dedicated pool smoke-tests).
final_checks_before_close: Confirm all fallback-log entries have owner and initial RCA assigned
Merge telemetry sampling changes into observability mainline (PR number recorded)
Close any temporary feature flags and annotate rollout in the model catalog
Send post-deploy summary to customer-success and ops-all
